title: Psalms 119: chapter overview
paragraphs: This psalm may be considered as the statement of a believer's experience.
To original corruption all have added actual sin.
If God deals in strict justice with us, we all perish.
While the souls of the children of this world cleave to the earth as their portion, the children of light are greatly burdened, because of the remains of carnal affections in their hearts.
Teach me thy statutes, not the mere words, but the way of applying them to myself.
Lord, I have by faith thy mercies in view; let me by prayer prevail to obtain them.
Those that make God's promises their portion, may with humble boldness make them their plea.
True believers take the Lord for the portion of their inheritance, and nothing less will satisfy them.
However God has dealt with us, he has dealt with us better than we deserve; and all in love, and for our good.
God made us to serve him, and enjoy him; but by sin we have made ourselves unfit to serve him, and to enjoy him.
The psalmist sought deliverance from his sins, his foes, and his fears.
The settling of God's word in heaven, is opposed to the changes and revolutions of the earth.
What we love, we love to think of.
The word of God directs us in our work and way, and a dark place indeed the world would be without it.
Here is a dread of the risings of sin, and the first beginnings of it.
Happy is the man, who, acting upon gospel principles, does justice to all around.
The wonders of redeeming love will fix the heart in adoration of them.
God never did, and never can do wrong to any.
Supplications with the whole heart are presented only by those who desire God's salvation, and who love his commandments.
The closer we cleave to the word of God, both as our rule and as our stay, the more assurance we have of deliverance.
Those whose hearts stand in awe of God's word, will rather endure the wrath of man, than break the law of God.
The psalmist desired grace and strength to lift up his prayers, and that the Lord would receive and notice them.
